week.weeklyOverview: This week toddlers go on a pretend camping adventure under the stars—no real fire. They build blanket tents, pack backpacks, explore woodland textures, follow a gentle bear hunt, and use battery flashlights with eye-safe habits. Days stay short and sensory: nature treasures, star stickers, owl flight movement, and campfire stories around battery lanterns or red/yellow tissue “flames.” Teachers expect parallel play, brief attention, and lots of repetition with tent, hike, star, and gentle night words.
week.objectives:
Social-emotional: Practice cooperative camping roles, turn-taking, and cozy group story moments.
Language: Hear and try camping words such as tent, campfire (pretend), flashlight, trail, stars, owl, bear, and hike.
Cognitive: Notice nature treasures and follow simple exploration sequences.
Fine motor: Pack large items, stamp tracks, place star stickers, and collage with big nature props.
Gross motor: Crawl into tents, follow obstacle trails, and soar like owls in short movement games.
Sensory: Explore woodland bins, glow-star play, and safe flashlight light/dark contrast.
Creative: Process nature collages, camping badges, and open-ended campsite building.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Everyday: blankets, chairs/clips for tent, backpacks, large nature props (pinecones, leaves), stuffed forest animals, blocks, boxes, painter’s tape, smocks, towels
Light/safety: battery flashlights/lanterns only (no candles/real fire); red/yellow tissue or LED tea lights for pretend campfire
Art: washable paint, paper, large star stickers, stampers, glue sticks, pre-cut badge circles
Sensory: shallow tubs, leaves, pinecones (large), scoops, optional safe glow items
Dramatic play: pretend fishing poles (soft), binoculars, explorer badges, camp dishes
Literacy: Pete the Cat Goes Camping; We’re Going on a Bear Hunt; Curious George Goes Camping; Twinkle Twinkle Little Star board book; optional Llama Llama Loves Camping
Optional printables: trail signs; day/night cards
week.teacherPreparation:
Before Monday: stage a reusable blanket tent; test battery lights; remove real-fire props.
Prep woodland sensory filler and large nature props (no tiny sticks).
Create a pretend campfire from tissue/LED only.
Choose 2–3 camping books.
Print trail/campsite signs if using.
Review flashlight eye-safety: never shine in eyes; model pointing at floor/walls.
prepChecklist: Sanitize forest animals and nature props
week.observationFocus:
Willingness to enter cozy tent spaces
Camping vocabulary attempts
Flashlight safety habits with support
Turn-taking on trails and sensory bins
Sensory preferences with nature textures
Listening during bear hunt/story cues
week.familyConnection: Invite families to make a blanket fort at home or look for stars/moon from a window and name one camping word together (tent, star, hike). Optional backyard picnic—no homework required.
week.adaptations: Offer watching-first entry to tents, dim-not-dark rooms, dry alternatives to messy nature play, shorter trails, and picture supports. Never force dark spaces or flashlight use.

activities.imageBriefSetup: Toddler blanket tent campsite with cushions and battery lantern pretend campfire tray. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Set Up the Campsite
activities.objective: Collaborate to arrange a toddler campsite with a blanket tent, pretend campfire, and cozy sitting spots.
activities.description: Toddlers help drape blankets, place cushions, and arrange a battery lantern or tissue-flame campfire ring—building the home base for the week.
activities.materials:
2 chairs or low table + clips
Blankets/sheets
Cushions
Battery lantern or LED tea lights
Red/yellow tissue paper “flames”
Stuffed forest friends
Basket of camp dishes
activities.preparation:
Test blanket stability
Confirm NO real flame props
Stage materials in a basket
activities.setup: Clear corner. Chairs stable. Fire ring on a tray away from blanket edges.
activities.steps:
1. Show the camping picture or chant: “We’re setting up camp!”
2. Invite toddlers to help spread the blanket tent.
3. Place cushions inside/outside.
4. Build pretend campfire on a tray (tissue/LED only).
5. Sit together and say “Campsite ready!”
6. Practice gentle entry/exit from the tent.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Can you help with the blanket?
Is the tent cozy?
Glow light — battery safe.
Sit by the pretend fire.
Our campsite is ready!
activities.observationOpportunities: Helping behaviors, willingness to enter tent, spatial arranging, and camping vocabulary.
activities.safetyNotes: No real fire/candles/matches. Stable chairs. Supervise tent play—keep exits clear. Battery lights only.
activities.cleanupTips: Fold blankets loosely for reuse; collect lanterns; reset fire tray.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Table tent with a sheet if chairs are limited.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Shade-structure tent with blankets under a tree.
teacherTips: Keep tent tall enough to sit, not a closed cave.

substitutions.use: Crib sheet over a low table with open sides

activities.adaptations: Offer a peek-in first. Keep one side fully open. Dim room rather than dark.
activities.extensions: Add a backpack landing spot beside the tent.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers clip blankets; younger place cushions.
observationPrompts: Did the child help place a campsite item?
Did they enter or sit near the tent?

activities.imageBriefSetup: Open-sided blanket tent with cushions and toddler stuffed animal inside. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Tent Exploration
activities.objective: Explore the tent space freely—look, crawl, sit, and notice in/out and light/cozy feelings.
activities.description: Toddlers crawl in and out of the open blanket tent, carry a stuffed friend inside, and notice how the space feels different from the open room.
activities.materials:
Prepared blanket tent (open sides)
1–2 stuffed animals
Soft flashlight optional (battery)
Cushions
activities.preparation:
Ensure open exit
Sanitize cushions
Set “open” visual on tent door
activities.setup: Tent with clear doorway; teacher seated nearby at toddler level.
activities.steps:
1. Invite: “Want to visit the tent?”
2. Model crawling in with a stuffed friend.
3. Allow free in/out exploration.
4. Offer words: in, out, cozy, dark/light.
5. Wave flashlight on the ceiling/floor only if used.
6. Come out for a stretch.
activities.teacherLanguage:
In the tent?
Is it cozy?
Your bear can come too.
Light on the floor — not eyes.
Out we go!
activities.observationOpportunities: Comfort with enclosed spaces, spatial language, and peer proximity in small spaces.
activities.safetyNotes: Keep exits clear. No overcrowding (1–2 children). Flashlight never in eyes. Continuous supervision.
activities.cleanupTips: Fluff cushions; air out blankets.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Chair fort if tent is busy—second cozy spot.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Play tunnel on grass as a tent alternative.
teacherTips: Narrate for watchers outside the tent.

substitutions.use: Large cardboard box house with open door

activities.adaptations: Sit at the doorway together. Keep lights brighter for sensitive children.
activities.extensions: Deliver a “mail” leaf to someone inside the tent.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants peek with caregiver; older toddlers host a friend.
observationPrompts: Did the child enter, peek, or play nearby?
Did they use in/out or cozy words?

activities.title: Campfire Songs
activities.objective: Share short camping songs around a pretend campfire with finger twinkles and gentle sway movements.
activities.description: Toddlers sit near the tissue/LED campfire and sing Twinkle Twinkle and a simple camping chant with scarf sways—no real fire heat.
activities.materials:
Pretend campfire tray
Scarves
Song card prompts
Optional battery lantern
activities.preparation:
Set fire tray safely
Choose 2 songs max
Plan seated movements
activities.setup: Semi-circle of cushions facing the pretend fire.
activities.steps:
1. Gather at the glow.
2. Twinkle fingers to Twinkle Twinkle.
3. Sway scarves like night wind.
4. Soft camping chant with pack motions.
5. Blow a pretend “goodnight” to the glow (LED stays on teacher control).
activities.teacherLanguage:
Twinkle fingers!
Glow, glow little light.
Sway like the trees.
Quiet campfire voices.
Goodnight, glow.
activities.observationOpportunities: Song participation, imitation of gestures, and calm group attention.
activities.safetyNotes: Battery/LED only. Scarves away from faces if mouthing. Seated bodies near tray.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect scarves; store lantern.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Same songs without props if fire tray is put away.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Evening-feel shade songs outdoors with lantern.
teacherTips: Offer silent finger twinkles for shy singers.

substitutions.use: Paper plate “moons” on sticks to sway

activities.adaptations: Lap sitting with caregiver. Humming instead of singing.
activities.extensions: Let a child hold the lantern (teacher-supervised) for one verse.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers suggest the next song; younger sway.
observationPrompts: Did the child attempt twinkle motions?
Did they remain near the group for a song?

activities.imageBriefSetup: Packing station with open toddler tote, cup, blanket square, and stuffed animal. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Pack the Backpack
activities.objective: Practice packing and unpacking large camping items to build bilateral coordination and care routines.
activities.description: Toddlers fit a cup, soft blanket square, and stuffed animal into an open backpack or tote, then unpack at the campsite.
activities.materials:
Toddler backpacks or open totes
Cup
Small soft blanket
Stuffed animal
Optional picture packing list (3 icons)
activities.preparation:
Use wide-mouth bags
Limit to 3 large items
Stage unpack spot
activities.setup: Packing station table + campsite unpack cushion.
activities.steps:
1. Show picture list: cup, blanket, friend.
2. Model pack one item.
3. Child packs remaining items.
4. Carry bag to campsite (short walk).
5. Unpack and check the list.
6. Repack for the next friend.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What do we pack?
Cup in!
Blanket in!
Is Bear ready?
Unpack at camp.
You packed it!
activities.observationOpportunities: Fitting objects, sequencing with pictures, carrying, and unpacking follow-through.
activities.safetyNotes: No tiny packing items. Soft materials. Supervise straps (no neck wrapping).
activities.cleanupTips: Return items to supply basket; hang bags.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Pack a basket instead of backpack.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Pack and walk a short outdoor loop.
teacherTips: Wide totes beat complicated zippers for 12–18 months.
Celebrate any item that goes in.

substitutions.use: Paper grocery bag with handles or beach tote

activities.adaptations: Offer one item only. Hand-under-hand packing.
activities.extensions: Add a fourth item for older toddlers (hat).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Preschoolers zip; toddlers choose what goes in.
observationPrompts: Did the child place at least one item in the bag?
Did they unpack at camp?

activities.title: Camping Story Corner
activities.objective: Build camping vocabulary and cozy listening through a short tent-side read-aloud.
activities.description: Teacher reads Pete the Cat Goes Camping or Curious George Goes Camping beside the tent with a lantern glow and pausing for pointing.
activities.materials:
Pete the Cat Goes Camping and/or Curious George Goes Camping
Lantern (battery)
Cushions
1 camping prop (cup or hat)
activities.preparation:
Preview pages
Keep group small
Plan 2–3 prompts
activities.setup: Cushions by tent door; lantern on floor lighting pages (not eyes).
activities.steps:
1. Show cover and prop.
2. Read slowly with pauses.
3. Invite pointing to tent/pack pictures.
4. Connect to your classroom tent.
5. Close book and pat the tent “goodnight.”
activities.teacherLanguage:
Where is the tent?
What did they pack?
Our tent looks cozy too.
Your turn to point.
Goodnight, story.
activities.observationOpportunities: Joint attention, pointing, book interest, and connections to the campsite.
activities.safetyNotes: Battery light only. Stable seating. Board books preferred.
activities.cleanupTips: Return books; power off lantern.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Lap reading away from tent if space is busy.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Shade story with the same book.
teacherTips: Short sessions beat finishing every page.
Hold book low for toddler sightlines.
activities.adaptations: One-on-one reading. Photo cards if book is overstimulating.
activities.extensions: Match a story prop to the real campsite item.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers turn pages; younger point and listen.
observationPrompts: Did the child point to a picture?
Did they connect story to the classroom tent?

activities.imageBriefSetup: Green fabric forest rug with basket of large stuffed forest animals. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Forest Animal Discovery
activities.objective: Meet forest animals through touch and naming—bear, owl, raccoon, deer—as camping neighbors.
activities.description: Toddlers explore a basket of large stuffed/plastic forest animals on a “forest rug,” choosing favorites and practicing gentle touch.
activities.materials:
4–6 large forest animals
Green rug or fabric “forest”
Basket
Optional animal photo cards
activities.preparation:
Sanitize animals
Limit set size
Remove tiny accessories
activities.setup: Forest fabric on floor with open basket.
activities.steps:
1. Greet one animal: “Hello, bear.”
2. Invite choosing/holding.
3. Model gentle pats.
4. Offer simple sounds if children initiate.
5. Rest animals in the forest basket.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Who lives in the forest?
Gentle bear.
Owl soft wings?
Which friend will you hold?
Animals rest now.
activities.observationOpportunities: Animal preference, naming attempts, gentle touch, and approach/avoid patterns.
activities.safetyNotes: Large animals only. Sanitize after mouthing. Supervise.
activities.cleanupTips: Basket animals; shake forest fabric.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Tabletop discovery if floor is crowded.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Forest animal picnic on an outdoor blanket.
activities.adaptations: Hand-under-hand gentle touch. Identical pairs if sharing is hard.
activities.extensions: Walk animals to the tent for a visit.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers introduce animals by name to younger friends.
observationPrompts: Did the child choose an animal?
Did they attempt a name or gentle touch?

activities.imageBriefSetup: Woodland sensory tub with leaves, large pinecones, scoops, and forest animals. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Woodland Sensory Bin
activities.objective: Explore woodland textures—leaves, large pinecones, scoops—while finding hidden forest animals.
activities.description: Toddlers dig in a shallow bin of leaves/paper leaves and large pinecones to scoop and discover animals.
activities.materials:
Shallow tub
Large leaves (real clean or faux) / paper leaves
Large pinecones
2–3 animals
Scoops
Smocks
Towel
activities.preparation:
Allergy check (pollen/mold on real leaves)
Use large pinecones only
Hide animals
activities.setup: Tub on towel; 2 children; wipe station ready.
activities.steps:
1. Feel a leaf together.
2. Scoop and pour.
3. Find a hidden animal.
4. Name textures: dry, bumpy, soft.
5. Wash/wipe hands.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What do you feel?
Bumpy pinecone.
Can you find the owl?
Scoop the leaves.
Wipe hands — all done.
activities.observationOpportunities: Sensory tolerance, scooping, searching, and texture vocabulary.
activities.safetyNotes: No tiny sticks/berries. Supervise pinecones (no mouthing sharp scales—redirect). Floor slip control.
activities.cleanupTips: Dispose of dirty real leaves; sanitize animals; sweep.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Paper leaves + fabric scraps only.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Nature table outdoors with fresh large treasures (teacher-vetted).

substitutions.use: Cork pieces or large wooden rings

activities.adaptations: Tools-only play. Separate personal tray.
activities.extensions: Sort leaves vs pinecones into two bowls.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older hide animals; younger find.
observationPrompts: Did the child scoop or dig?
Did they notice a texture word with support?

activities.title: Bear Hunt Adventure
activities.objective: Follow a simple bear-hunt path with movement cues inspired by We’re Going on a Bear Hunt—keeping the adventure playful, not scary.
activities.description: Toddlers tip-toe through “grass,” step on cushions “mud,” crawl under a scarf “cave,” then tip-toe back when they spot the bear (stuffed).
activities.materials:
We’re Going on a Bear Hunt (optional cue)
Painter’s tape path
Grass scarves
Cushions
Scarf cave
Stuffed bear
Open space
activities.preparation:
Keep story playful
Set 3 stations only
Place bear visibly at end (not jump-scare)
activities.setup: Linear path: grass → mud → cave → bear wave → tip-toe home.
activities.steps:
1. Chant softly: going on a bear hunt.
2. Swish through scarf grass.
3. Step on cushion mud.
4. Crawl under cave.
5. Wave to bear — “Hi, bear!”
6. Tip-toe back to camp.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Going on a bear hunt!
Swish, swish grass.
Squish mud.
Under the cave.
Hi, bear!
Tip-toe home.
activities.observationOpportunities: Path following, movement imitation, bravery with support, and listening to cues.
activities.safetyNotes: No scary hides. Soft obstacles. Spot crawlers. Walking feet.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect scarves/cushions; return bear to forest basket.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Seated hand motions version of the hunt.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Outdoor landmark hunt between trees.
activities.adaptations: Skip cave for hesitant children. Watcher role with chanting.
activities.extensions: Child places the bear for the next group.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers lead chant; younger move with teacher.
observationPrompts: Did the child attempt the path?
Did they greet the bear or tip-toe back?

activities.imageBriefExample: Toddler paper trail with large painted animal track stamps. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Animal Track Stamping
activities.objective: Make large animal tracks with stampers or plastic animal feet—process printmaking, not worksheets.
activities.description: Toddlers press large stampers or plastic animal feet into washable paint and stamp tracks across paper “trails.”
activities.materials:
Large paper
Washable paint on trays
Track stampers or plastic animals with flat feet
Smocks
Wipes
activities.preparation:
Pour thin paint
Tape paper
Choose large stampers only
activities.setup: Art table for 2; trail paper long enough for walking hands.
activities.steps:
1. Show a track sample.
2. Model dip and press.
3. Invite stamping anywhere on the trail.
4. Name animals if child is interested.
5. Wash hands.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Dip and press!
Tracks on the trail.
More stamps?
Whose tracks?
You made footprints!
activities.observationOpportunities: Press force, bilateral use, interest in trails, and animal talk.
activities.safetyNotes: Non-toxic paint. Supervise plastic animals. Smocks.
activities.cleanupTips: Wash stampers; dry art; wipe table.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Stamp on coffee filters if paper is short.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Water stamp tracks on sidewalk (wet prints).
activities.adaptations: One color only. Pre-loaded stamper.
activities.extensions: Follow the tracks with a finger hike.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers make a path story; younger stamp freely.
observationPrompts: Did the child stamp intentionally?
Did they notice tracks as footprints?

activities.title: Forest Animal Pretend Play
activities.objective: Act out simple forest animal roles—sleeping bears, flying owls—in short pretend scenes near the tent.
activities.description: Toddlers choose an animal friend and act out sleep, eat, or fly using blankets and the tent as a den.
activities.materials:
Forest animals
Blankets
Tent
Bowls for pretend food
Optional ear headbands (soft, large)
activities.preparation:
Limit props
Stage den and eating spots
Sanitize headbands if used
activities.setup: Den blanket nest, pretend eating spot, and open fly space near the tent.
activities.steps:
1. Choose an animal role.
2. Bear sleeps in den.
3. Wake and pretend eat.
4. Owl arm-flaps in fly space.
5. Animals rest together.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Is your bear sleepy?
Night-night in the den.
Time to eat.
Owl wings flap!
Rest, forest friends.
activities.observationOpportunities: Role play attempts, sequence play, peer awareness, and animal vocabulary.
activities.safetyNotes: Soft headbands only; supervise. No small costume parts.
activities.cleanupTips: Fold den blankets; return animals.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Table den under a sheet.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Tree-shade dens outdoors.
teacherTips: Join briefly as a co-animal then step back.
activities.adaptations: One action only (sleep). Watching with narration.
activities.extensions: Visit another child’s den with a gentle knock.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers assign roles; younger follow one action.
observationPrompts: Did the child act out at least one animal action?
Did they use den/sleep/fly words?

activities.imageBriefSetup: Treasure basket with large leaves and pinecones beside picture cards on a short trail. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Nature Treasure Hunt
activities.objective: Search for large nature treasures on a short indoor/outdoor hunt and collect them in a basket.
activities.description: Toddlers hunt for teacher-placed large leaves, pinecones, and smooth stones (too big to choke), placing finds in a treasure basket.
activities.materials:
Basket
Large leaves
Large pinecones
Smooth large stones (optional)
Picture treasure cards
Trail markers
activities.preparation:
Vet all treasures for size/safety
Place 5–6 items visibly
Allergy awareness outdoors
activities.setup: Short loop with obvious treasures; teacher spots along the path.
activities.steps:
1. Show a treasure card.
2. Hunt with eyes and fingers.
3. Place find in basket.
4. Name color/texture.
5. Return to camp to admire the collection.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Can you find a leaf?
Treasure!
In the basket.
Bumpy or smooth?
Look at our nature treasures.
activities.observationOpportunities: Searching persistence, matching to pictures, carrying, and nature vocabulary.
activities.safetyNotes: Treasures larger than choke tube. No berries/fungi. Wash hands after outdoor hunt.
activities.cleanupTips: Sort keepers vs compost; wash stones; sanitize baskets.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Hide treasures around the classroom “forest.”
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Playground edge hunt with teacher-vetted items only.
teacherTips: Hide in plain sight for toddlers.
activities.adaptations: Offer a paired hunt with teacher pointing. One treasure goal.
activities.extensions: Sort treasures by color on a towel.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers hide for younger finders.
observationPrompts: Did the child find and collect an item?
Did they use look/find words?

activities.imageBriefSetup: Investigation trays with leaves, large pinecones, and plastic magnifier. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Leaf and Pinecone Investigation
activities.objective: Investigate nature props with looking, touching, and simple comparing (big/little, bumpy/smooth).
activities.description: Toddlers examine leaves and large pinecones on trays, using fingers and optional plastic magnifiers while teachers narrate features.
activities.materials:
Trays
Leaves
Large pinecones
Plastic magnifiers
Sorting bowls
Wipes
activities.preparation:
Clean props
Select varied leaf sizes
Sanitize magnifiers
activities.setup: Side-by-side investigation trays with leaves, pinecones, and optional magnifiers for 2 toddlers.
activities.steps:
1. Feel a leaf — “thin.”
2. Feel pinecone — “bumpy.”
3. Look with magnifier (optional).
4. Sort into two bowls.
5. Wash hands.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What do you feel?
Bumpy pinecone.
Big leaf or little leaf?
Look closely.
Two piles — sort!
activities.observationOpportunities: Tactile exploration, comparing language, sorting attempts, and attention span.
activities.safetyNotes: Large props only. Supervise magnifiers. No tasting nature props.
activities.cleanupTips: Wipe trays; store dry props.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Fabric leaf set if real leaves unavailable.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Investigate on a park bench with teacher-selected items.
activities.adaptations: Tools-only. Pre-sorted starting piles.
activities.extensions: Make a leaf sound by gentle crumpling (over a bin).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers describe; younger feel and sort with cues.
observationPrompts: Did the child touch and compare props?
Did they attempt bumpy/smooth or big/little?

activities.title: Hiking Trail Obstacle Course
activities.objective: Hike a short obstacle trail—step, crawl, and balance—building gross-motor confidence for explorers.
activities.description: Toddlers follow trail signs along a path: over a cushion hill, under a scarf bridge, and around a cone tree, then rest at a lookout.
activities.materials:
Trail arrow signs
Cushions
Scarves
Cone
Backpack optional
Finish lookout cushion
activities.preparation:
Clear hazards
Keep obstacles low
Mark one-way trail
activities.setup: One-way 3-station trail ending at a lookout cushion with arrow signs visible.
activities.steps:
1. Put on pretend hiking feet.
2. Follow arrows.
3. Step over hill.
4. Crawl under bridge.
5. Walk around tree cone.
6. Sit at lookout and “see the forest.”
activities.teacherLanguage:
Hiking time!
Follow the arrow.
Over the hill.
Under the bridge.
Around the tree.
Lookout rest!
activities.observationOpportunities: Balance, climbing-over, directional following, and stamina for short courses.
activities.safetyNotes: Spot children. No running. Soft obstacles only.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect signs and scarves.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Hallway hike with tape arrows.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Playground hike between landmarks.
teacherTips: Offer a wagon for tired hikers’ backpacks.
activities.adaptations: Hand-holding. Skip crawl station. Shorter trail.
activities.extensions: Child places the next arrow.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers add a balance beam line of tape; younger walk the path.
observationPrompts: Did the child complete at least two stations?
Did they follow an arrow cue?

activities.imageBriefExample: Toddler nature collage with large leaves and paper shapes on cardboard. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Nature Collage Creation
activities.objective: Create process nature collages with large leaves, paper shapes, and glue sticks—no tiny crafts or worksheets.
activities.description: Toddlers stick large nature props and paper shapes onto cardboard to make open-ended forest collages.
activities.materials:
Cardboard sheets
Glue sticks
Large leaves (faux/real clean)
Pre-cut paper shapes
Smocks
Optional large stickers
activities.preparation:
Pre-cut shapes
Prep glue sticks loosened
Tape cardboard to table
activities.setup: Art table for 2 with cardboard taped down and nature pieces in easy-reach bowls.
activities.steps:
1. Choose cardboard.
2. Glue a leaf or shape.
3. Add more freely.
4. Talk about sticky/press.
5. Admire and set to dry.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Sticky glue!
Press the leaf.
Another shape?
Your forest collage.
All done?
activities.observationOpportunities: Glue-stick control, creative placement, persistence, and nature talk.
activities.safetyNotes: Large materials only. Non-toxic glue. Supervise real leaves.
activities.cleanupTips: Cap glue; dry flat; discard crumbling leaves.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Sticker-only nature collage.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Contact-paper nature catchers outdoors (teacher holds sticky side).
teacherTips: Offer contact paper sticky-side up for easier sticking.
activities.adaptations: Pre-dotted glue spots to press onto. Fewer choices.
activities.extensions: Add a star sticker night sky after drying.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers tear paper shapes; younger press ready pieces.
observationPrompts: Did the child stick at least one item?
Did they press/glue with intent?

activities.imageBriefSetup: Explorer station with badges, toy binoculars, picture map, and backpack. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Explorer Station
activities.objective: Role-play explorers using binoculars, maps (picture), and backpacks for short discovery missions.
activities.description: Toddlers wear explorer badges, look through toy binoculars, point on a simple picture map, and take a two-step mission to find a nature treasure.
activities.materials:
Explorer badges
Toy binoculars
Picture map (tent + tree icons)
Backpacks
1 treasure item
Clipboard with icons (no writing)
activities.preparation:
Remove binocular straps that can tighten; use short straps
Stage mission start at tent
activities.setup: Explorer table + short mission path to treasure.
activities.steps:
1. Put on badge.
2. Check the picture map.
3. Look through binoculars at the “tree.”
4. Walk to find the treasure.
5. Return to report: “Found it!”
activities.teacherLanguage:
Are you an explorer?
Check the map.
Look through binoculars.
Find the treasure!
You did the mission.
activities.observationOpportunities: Role language, map pointing, mission follow-through, and carrying.
activities.safetyNotes: Binocular cords short/supervised. No small compass parts. Clear floors.
activities.cleanupTips: Hang binoculars; return badges.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Window “safari” looking for outdoor trees.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Real playground explorer mission.
teacherTips: Maps are pictures, not literacy tests.

substitutions.use: Two toilet-paper tubes taped as lookers (supervise)

activities.adaptations: One-step find only. Teacher carries backpack.
activities.extensions: Draw an X on the map with a large crayon (optional).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers create missions; younger complete finds.
observationPrompts: Did the child use binoculars or badge in play?
Did they complete a simple find mission?

activities.imageBriefSetup: Dim classroom corner with toddler flashlight pointed at wall stars—not faces. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Flashlight Exploration
activities.objective: Explore light and dark safely with battery flashlights—pointing at walls/floors and noticing spots of light.
activities.description: In a dim (not pitch-dark) room, toddlers shine battery flashlights on walls, ceilings, and teacher-placed paper stars—practicing eye-safe habits.
activities.materials:
Battery flashlights (toddler-friendly)
Paper stars on walls
Dim light source still available
Blanket tent optional
activities.preparation:
Test batteries
Dim lights but keep safety lighting
Review “lights on walls/floors, not faces”
activities.setup: Clear floor; stars at toddler height; teacher models first.
activities.steps:
1. Model: light on the wall — not eyes.
2. Give flashlight to one toddler at a time (or pairs with space).
3. Find a star with the light.
4. Make light dance on the floor.
5. Power off and praise safe shining.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Light on the wall.
Not in eyes — safe light.
Can you find a star?
Dance the light.
Flashlight off — thank you.
activities.observationOpportunities: Safe aiming with support, visual tracking, turn-taking with popular tools, and night vocabulary.
activities.safetyNotes: Battery only. Never shine in eyes. Dim not dark. Supervise cords/buttons. Limit group size.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect flashlights; check batteries; restore room lights.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Light table or LED tap lights if flashlights are too stimulating.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Dusk outdoor flashlight walk on school grounds with high ratios.
teacherTips: Offer a teacher-shared flashlight for hesitant children.
activities.adaptations: Keep room brighter. Teacher holds light while child points where to shine.
activities.extensions: Trace a circle of light around a stuffed owl.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers help younger aim at stars.
observationPrompts: Did the child aim at wall/floor with support?
Did they follow the eye-safety reminder?

activities.imageBriefSetup: Dark-paper sensory bin with large star cutouts, scoops, and lantern nearby. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Glow Star Sensory Play
activities.objective: Explore glow-in-the-dark or shiny star sensory materials with scooping in a shallow night-sky bin.
activities.description: Toddlers scoop large star shapes, shiny foil pieces, and soft pom-poms in a dark-blue paper-lined bin—optionally with a gentle lantern glow nearby.
activities.materials:
Shallow tub lined with dark paper
Large star cutouts / star ice cubes (water play alternate)
Large shiny foil pieces
Scoops
Battery lantern
Smocks
activities.preparation:
No tiny glitter
Large stars only
Test lantern glow
activities.setup: Shallow night-sky bin for 2 toddlers with lantern glowing beside (not inside) the bin.
activities.steps:
1. Notice the “night sky” bin.
2. Scoop stars.
3. Crinkle shiny pieces.
4. Use words: shiny, star, night.
5. Clean hands.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Night sky bin!
Scoop a star.
Shiny!
Glow lantern beside us.
All done scooping?
activities.observationOpportunities: Sensory preference for shiny/soft, scooping, and night vocabulary.
activities.safetyNotes: No loose glitter. Large pieces only. Supervise foil (no mouthing large amounts).
activities.cleanupTips: Flatten foil for reuse; store stars; wipe bin.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Dry star sticker peeling station if bin is too much.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Water table star floating outdoors.

substitutions.use: Yellow paper stars and aluminum foil moons

activities.adaptations: Personal tray. Tools-only.
activities.extensions: Stick one wet star on a window overnight (teacher).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers count stars casually; younger scoop.
observationPrompts: Did the child scoop or explore shiny textures?
Did they use star/night words?

activities.title: Owl Flight Movement Game
activities.objective: Move like owls—arm wing flaps, quiet tip-toe flights, and freeze perches—to build listening and body control.
activities.description: Toddlers flap “wings,” tip-toe fly across a path, and freeze on cushion “perches” when the owl call stops.
activities.materials:
Open space
Cushion perches
Soft owl call cue (voice or shaker)
Optional owl picture
activities.preparation:
Place 3–4 perches
Clear path
Practice soft cue
activities.setup: Path between perches with space to flap.
activities.steps:
1. Show owl wings (arms).
2. Flap and tip-toe fly.
3. Freeze on a perch when cue stops.
4. Quiet owl eyes look around.
5. Fly back to the nest rug.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Flap your owl wings!
Quiet tip-toe flight.
Perch — freeze!
Big owl eyes.
Back to the nest.
activities.observationOpportunities: Imitation, freeze listening, balance on cushions, and gentle movement control.
activities.safetyNotes: Space out. Soft landings. No jumping from heights.
activities.cleanupTips: Stack cushions.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Seated wing flaps if energy is high.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Owl flights across the playground.
activities.adaptations: Hand-holding flights. Sit-to-flap option.
activities.extensions: Child makes the freeze call.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants watch wing flaps; older toddlers lead.
observationPrompts: Did the child flap or tip-toe?
Did they attempt to freeze on cue?

activities.imageBriefExample: Dark paper with large toddler-placed star stickers. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Star Sticker Art
activities.objective: Strengthen fine-motor peeling and placing by decorating night paper with large star stickers.
activities.description: Toddlers peel large star stickers and place them on dark paper skies—process placement, not precise constellations.
activities.materials:
Dark construction paper
Large star stickers
Optional crayon for moon scribbles
Wipes
activities.preparation:
Loosen sticker corners
Pre-cut paper
Avoid tiny star confetti
activities.setup: Art table; sticker sheets shared carefully.
activities.steps:
1. Show night paper.
2. Model peel and stick.
3. Invite free star placement.
4. Optional moon scribble.
5. Count stars casually if interest.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Peel the star.
Stick on the night!
More stars?
Yellow star.
Your sky is shiny.
activities.observationOpportunities: Pincer peel attempts, sticker placement, persistence, and night talk.
activities.safetyNotes: Large stickers only. Supervise mouthing. No glitter glue.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect backing paper; store extras; display art.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Star stamps if stickers frustrate.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Chalk stars on pavement.
teacherTips: Start stickers for children who can’t peel yet.

substitutions.use: Star foam shapes with glue dots

activities.adaptations: Pre-peeled stickers to press. Hand-under-hand peel.
activities.extensions: Add a flashlight glow to admire art in dim light.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers make patterns; younger place freely.
observationPrompts: Did the child place a sticker?
Did they attempt peeling?

activities.imageBriefSetup: Cushion circle around pretend campfire tray with battery lantern and book. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Campfire Story Time
activities.objective: Combine cozy pretend campfire gathering with storytelling roles—listener, teller, and lantern helper.
activities.description: Toddlers sit by the pretend campfire with a battery lantern while the teacher tells a short camping tale or reads We’re Going on a Bear Hunt excerpts, inviting toddlers to add sounds.
activities.materials:
Pretend campfire tray
Battery lantern
We’re Going on a Bear Hunt or short oral story
Cushions
Optional sound props (rain stick soft)
activities.preparation:
Keep story gentle
Charge/check lantern
Limit group size for coziness
activities.setup: Campfire circle; lantern center; book ready.
activities.steps:
1. Gather with soft voices.
2. Turn lantern glow on.
3. Tell/read short story with sound cues.
4. Invite toddlers to swish/splash sounds.
5. End with quiet twinkle fingers.
6. Lantern off — bedtime for camp.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Campfire story time.
Soft voices.
What sound do we hear?
Swish through grass.
Twinkle goodnight.
Lantern off.
activities.observationOpportunities: Listening, sound participation, comfort in group circle, and pretend camping engagement.
activities.safetyNotes: Battery lantern only. No real fire. Soft seating. Supervise props.
activities.cleanupTips: Power off lantern; reset cushions.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Story without lantern if overstimulating.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Shade campfire circle outdoors.
activities.adaptations: Lap seating. Shorter oral story only.
activities.extensions: Child holds lantern for the final twinkle (supervised).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers add story lines; younger make sounds.
observationPrompts: Did the child attend to part of the story?
Did they add a sound or gesture?

activities.imageBriefSetup: Pretend blue pond with large fish, toddler scoop/pole, and catch basket. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Pretend Fishing Adventure
activities.objective: Practice scooping and catching with toddler fishing poles or cups at a pretend pond—large fish only.
activities.description: Toddlers “fish” in a blue fabric/water bin pond using magnetic or scoop poles to catch large foam/plastic fish, then place catches in a basket.
activities.materials:
Blue fabric or shallow water bin
Large fish props
Toddler fishing poles or scoops/cups
Catch basket
Towels if water used
activities.preparation:
Choose catch method that works (scoop often easier than magnets for 12–18 mo)
Large fish only
Decide dry vs wet pond
activities.setup: Blue pond on a towel with catch basket; limit to 2 fishers at a time.
activities.steps:
1. Show the pond.
2. Model scoop/catch.
3. Catch a fish.
4. Put fish in basket.
5. Throw fish back for friends (or keep for count).
6. Dry hands if wet.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Going fishing!
Scoop the fish.
You caught one!
In the basket.
Fish go back — splash!
activities.observationOpportunities: Hand-eye coordination, persistence, turn-taking, and fishing vocabulary.
activities.safetyNotes: No hooks. Large fish. Supervise water. Poles soft and short.
activities.cleanupTips: Dump water; dry fish; store poles.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Dry fabric pond with scoop cups.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Water table fishing outdoors.
teacherTips: Keep waiting basket of poles limited.
activities.adaptations: Hand-under-hand scooping. Pre-catch fish to place in basket.
activities.extensions: Sort big/little fish.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers use magnetic poles; younger scoop.
observationPrompts: Did the child catch or scoop a fish?
Did they place it in the basket?

activities.imageBriefSetup: Floor campground with blocks, box tents, tape paths, and forest animals. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Campground Building Challenge
activities.objective: Build an expanded campground with blocks, tents, and paths—open-ended construction celebrating the week.
activities.description: Toddlers add block paths, box tents, and animal visitors to create a whole campground map on the floor.
activities.materials:
Blocks
Small boxes
Blankets scraps
Animals
Tape paths
Lantern prop
activities.preparation:
Clear large floor space
Sort blocks
Keep paths wide
activities.setup: Large floor build zone with blocks and boxes staged around the edges for easy access.
activities.steps:
1. Recall the week’s campsite.
2. Build more tents/paths.
3. Place animals as campers.
4. Add a fishing pond fabric.
5. Take a visitor walk.
6. Clean-up song.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Can you build another tent?
Path to the pond!
Who is camping here?
Block on block.
Our campground is big!
activities.observationOpportunities: Construction ideas, spatial language, peer collaboration, and thematic connection.
activities.safetyNotes: Stable builds only. No tall towers. Supervise box tents.
activities.cleanupTips: Sort blocks; fold scraps; basket animals.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Tabletop campground for smaller groups.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Chalk campground map outdoors.
activities.adaptations: Pre-built tent to furnish. One building goal.
activities.extensions: Add ticket booth for parade later.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Preschoolers plan layout; toddlers place campers.
observationPrompts: Did the child add a structure or path?
Did they place a camper animal?

activities.title: Nature Dance Party
activities.objective: Celebrate nature and camping with a joyful dance party using scarves, stomps, and freeze dances.
activities.description: Toddlers dance with leaf scarves to upbeat nature-themed music, freeze like trees, then sway like wind.
activities.materials:
Scarves
Music player
Optional leaf props
Open space
activities.preparation:
Clear space
Choose 2 songs
Plan freeze cues
activities.setup: Open dance zone with scarves in a center basket and clear freeze-space markers.
activities.steps:
1. Scarves out — leaf dance.
2. Stomp like hiking boots.
3. Freeze like tall trees.
4. Sway in the wind.
5. Rest on the rug.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Dance like leaves!
Stomp, stomp hike.
Freeze — tall tree!
Sway in the wind.
Resting dancers.
activities.observationOpportunities: Rhythmic movement, freeze control, scarf play, and celebration joy.
activities.safetyNotes: Space out. Scarves off necks. Walking stomps indoors.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect scarves.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Seated scarf dances.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Outdoor dance party on grass.

substitutions.use: Drum beat and nature sounds playlist-free clapping

activities.adaptations: Lap bouncing dances. Slow music option.
activities.extensions: Child chooses freeze or dance.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers lead moves; younger scarf sway.
observationPrompts: Did the child dance or sway with a scarf?
Did they attempt freeze?

activities.imageBriefExample: Toddler-decorated camping badge with star stickers and crayon marks. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Make a Camping Badge
activities.objective: Create a large camping explorer badge with stickers and scribbles—wear or keep as a souvenir.
activities.description: Toddlers decorate pre-cut cardboard badge circles with star stickers, crayons, and glue-on paper tents—teacher attaches tape/pin-free sticky backs or yarn loops.
activities.materials:
Pre-cut cardboard circles
Large stickers
Crayons
Paper tent shapes
Glue sticks
Masking tape to attach to shirts (no sharp pins)
activities.preparation:
Pre-cut badges
Avoid pins/sharp fasteners
Loosen stickers
activities.setup: Art table; name labels ready for teacher to write.
activities.steps:
1. Choose a badge.
2. Decorate freely.
3. Add a star or tent shape.
4. Teacher tapes badge to shirt or offers to hold.
5. Proud explorer pose.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Your camping badge!
Stick a star.
Color the badge.
You are an explorer.
Show your badge!
activities.observationOpportunities: Decorating choices, fine motor, pride in sharing, and theme connection.
activities.safetyNotes: No pins. Large stickers. Tape attachments only. Supervise yarn loops.
activities.cleanupTips: Cap glue; label badges; store extras.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Paper badges if cardboard is scarce.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Decorate outdoors then parade.
teacherTips: Holding badge is fine if wearing bothers.
activities.adaptations: Pre-decorated badge to add one sticker. Hand-under-hand.
activities.extensions: Use badges as parade tickets.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers choose symbols; younger sticker freely.
observationPrompts: Did the child decorate the badge?
Did they show or wear it proudly?

activities.title: Camping Adventure Parade
activities.objective: Close the week with a camping parade—backpacks, badges, and favorite animals marching the trail back to camp.
activities.description: Toddlers wear badges, carry backpacks or animals, and parade along the tape trail to the tent for a final campfire glow goodbye.
activities.materials:
Badges
Backpacks/animals
Tape parade path
Lantern
Pretend campfire
Music optional
activities.preparation:
Clear path
Power lantern
Invite clappers if desired
activities.setup: Path from rug to tent; glow ready at end.
activities.steps:
1. Gear up with badge/animal.
2. Start parade march.
3. Wave to forest friends.
4. Arrive at tent glow.
5. Soft goodbye twinkle.
6. Unpack gear to baskets.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Parade to camp!
March, march.
Wave to the forest!
Glow goodbye.
Twinkle fingers.
What a camping week!
activities.observationOpportunities: Group participation, carrying gear, celebration closure, and theme recall.
activities.safetyNotes: Walking feet. Battery glow only. Space backpacks.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect gear; power off lights; fold tent for weekend or leave if reusing.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Seated parade passing animals hand-to-hand.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Outdoor loop parade ending at shade tent.
teacherTips: Photo the group if families allow.

substitutions.use: Stickers on shirts as parade tickets

activities.adaptations: Wagon riders as parade VIPs. Watcher waving role.
activities.extensions: Share one favorite memory word as children unpack.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers lead; younger hold animals and follow.
observationPrompts: Did the child join the parade path?
Did they participate in the goodbye glow?
